bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free at the parent level: the secretarial auditor records that no secured loan has been obtained from any bank or financial institution and none of the Company's property has been mortgaged or hypothecated, confirmed through the MCA portal
- Entry into a high-value specialty lipid market with a stated positioning on value-added products and customer-specific formulations
- Promoter-led executive management with long tenure (Managing Director appointed 01/02/2008)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Project execution risk on the MCT Oil plant - the company's entire growth case rests on an asset that is not yet built — Management explicitly flags procurement timelines, installation and commissioning schedules, availability of utilities, regulatory approvals, cost escalations and market conditions while the project is under implementation. Commercial production is only expected in Q4 FY2026-27, and every forward statement in the MD&A is conditioned on successful commissioning, so slippage in any of these directly delays the diversification the Board is relying on.
- Raw material price volatility in coconut oil and palm kernel oil — MCT Oil is manufactured primarily from coconut oil and palm kernel oil, and volatility in their prices is named both as a threat and as a monitored business risk. Because the feedstock is a traded agri-commodity and the output is sold into quality-regulated end markets, input swings hit margin before they can be passed through. Mitigation stated is strategic sourcing and inventory planning.
- Customer concentration — Listed by management among the key business risks it continuously monitors. No customer count or share of revenue is disclosed anywhere in the report, so the degree of dependence cannot be sized from this annual report - the risk is acknowledged but unquantified.
- Foreign exchange exposure and export competitiveness — Foreign exchange fluctuation is named as a monitored risk and, separately, as a threat that affects export competitiveness. The strategy explicitly depends on increasing exports to North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, so currency moves bear on both realisation and price position against global suppliers.
- Regulatory compliance and stringent international food-safety / pharmaceutical quality standards — Regulatory compliance in domestic and export markets is a stated risk, and stringent international food safety and pharmaceutical quality standards are a stated threat. The company itself frames GMP, HACCP, FSSC 22000 and ISO compliance as something still to be strengthened rather than already held, which makes qualification for regulated export markets a gating condition on the export strategy.
- Competition from established global manufacturers in a market the company has not yet entered — Increasing competition from global manufacturers is named as a threat. Crestchem is entering the specialty lipid market as a new producer with no commissioned capacity, so it will meet incumbents with existing scale, accreditations and customer approvals.
- Supply chain disruption and freight cost fluctuation — Named as a threat. Relevant on both sides of an export-oriented specialty ingredients model: imported or traded oleochemical feedstock inbound, and international shipping outbound to the North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific markets the company targets.
- Geopolitical uncertainty affecting international trade, plus technological change — Both are named among the key business risks management monitors. Geopolitical disruption bears on the export-led growth plan; technological change bears on a process business whose competitive position rests on producing high-purity and customised MCT grades.
- Environmental, health and safety compliance in a chemical manufacturing operation — Listed among monitored business risks, and the secretarial audit records 'Laws Applicable to Chemical Industry' as specifically applicable to the Company. Cited here as an operating-continuity and compliance risk, not as an ESG target.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Crestchem Limited continued to carry on its existing business operations during FY2025-26 while pursuing a strategic expansion into the specialty chemicals and nutraceutical ingredients sector. Its stated focus segment is specialty lipids, centred on Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil, a specialty lipid manufactured primarily from coconut oil and palm kernel oil and used in nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals, clinical nutrition, sports nutrition, infant nutrition, functional foods, cosmetics and personal care. The MCT Oil manufacturing project is being implemented through Oleo Biosciences Private Limited, Bengaluru, incorporated on 31 March 2026, with plant and machinery procurement and installation underway and commercial production expected in Q4 FY2026-27.

outlook.body:
- Diversify out of the existing business into specialty chemicals and nutraceutical ingredients, executed through the newly incorporated subsidiary Oleo Biosciences Private Limited, Bengaluru, which is set up specifically to manufacture Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil.
- Complete the MCT Oil manufacturing project on schedule - procurement, purchase and installation of plant and machinery, utilities and other equipment - and commission it so commercial production starts in Q4 FY2026-27.
- Address both domestic and international markets on commissioning, with emphasis on the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, food and personal care industries.
- Expand manufacturing capacity.
- Develop high-purity specialty MCT grades and customised / premium-grade MCT products.
- Increase exports, with regulated international markets named as the export opportunity.
- Invest in research and development.
- Strengthen quality systems to comply with international standards such as GMP, HACCP, FSSC 22000 and ISO certifications - explicitly framed as a lever for the export ambition.
- Focus on value-added products and customer-specific formulations within the specialty lipid segment rather than commodity volume.
- Pursue potential strategic alliances with domestic and overseas customers.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The single expansion programme in this annual report is the Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil manufacturing project. During FY2025-26 Crestchem incorporated Oleo Biosciences Private Limited, Bengaluru, on 31 March 2026 to implement it; the Board's report states an equity participation of 75%, while the secretarial audit report describes the same entity as a Wholly Owned Subsidiary. The subsidiary's registered office is at B-61/A, 2nd Cross, 3rd Stage, Peenya Small Industries, Bangalore North, Karnataka - 560058. The procurement, purchase and installation of plant and machinery, utilities and other manufacturing equipment is presently underway; management states the project is progressing in accordance with the implementation schedule. Subject to timely completion of installation, successful commissioning, statutory approvals and trial production, commercial production is expected to commence during the fourth quarter of FY2026-27. On commissioning the subsidiary proposes to serve both domestic and international markets, with emphasis on pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, food and personal care industries, and the Board expects the project to diversify the business portfolio and strengthen long-term growth prospects. Beyond this project the Company states a general intent to expand manufacturing capacity, develop high-purity specialty MCT grades and invest in research and development. No plant capacity, no project cost, no rupee capex quantum and no funding plan is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, and the Directors' report separately states there were no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position of the Company during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management states the outlook for the MCT Oil industry remains positive, with growing awareness of preventive healthcare, clinical nutrition and sports nutrition expected to drive sustained demand.
- Expansion in pharmaceutical manufacturing, increasing adoption of ketogenic diets and rising demand for functional ingredients are described as likely to provide significant growth opportunities.
- Growing demand from pharmaceutical and medical nutrition applications, coupled with increasing acceptance of clean-label ingredients, is expected to support long-term industry growth.
- India is described as emerging as an important manufacturing hub because of its expanding healthcare and food processing industries, with the Indian market presenting significant opportunity from pharmaceutical, nutraceutical and food processing growth plus increasing export potential.
- Increasing exports to North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific are listed as an opportunity, alongside expansion of the personal care and cosmetic industries and government initiatives promoting value-added specialty chemicals and food processing.
- Increasing consumer preference for healthier edible oils and specialty ingredients is cited as a demand driver.
- Management remains confident that upon successful commissioning the subsidiary will contribute meaningfully to long-term revenue growth and profitability - the entire growth narrative is contingent on a plant that has not yet been commissioned.
- Margin/cost narrative for the existing business: cost optimisation initiatives, efficient procurement practices and enhanced production planning are said to have contributed towards improved operating performance, and management states it remains committed to maintaining healthy profitability while pursuing sustainable growth.
- Named demand headwinds: volatility in coconut oil and palm kernel oil prices, supply chain disruptions and freight cost fluctuations, stringent international food safety and pharmaceutical quality standards, exchange rate fluctuations affecting export competitiveness, and increasing competition from global manufacturers.

Listed by management among the key business risks it continuously monitors. No customer count or share of revenue is disclosed anywhere in the report, so the degree of dependence cannot be sized from this annual report - the risk is acknowledged but unquantified.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Crestchem Limited is a Gujarat-incorporated chemicals company diversifying into specialty lipids, setting up Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil manufacturing through its Bengaluru subsidiary Oleo Biosciences Private Limited, in which it holds a 75% equity participation.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Crestchem Limited continued to carry on its existing business operations during FY2025-26 while pursuing a strategic expansion into the specialty chemicals and nutraceutical ingredients sector. Its stated focus segment is specialty lipids, centred on Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil, a specialty lipid manufactured primarily from coconut oil and palm kernel oil and used in nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals, clinical nutrition, sports nutrition, infant nutrition, functional foods, cosmetics and personal care. The MCT Oil manufacturing project is being implemented through Oleo Biosciences Private Limited, Bengaluru, incorporated on 31 March 2026, with plant and machinery procurement and installation underway and commercial production expected in Q4 FY2026-27.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Oleo Biosciences Private Limited — subsidiary: Incorporated 31 March 2026, registered office at B-61/A, 2nd Cross, 3rd Stage, Peenya Small Industries, Bangalore North, Karnataka - 560058. Set up to manufacture Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil; had not commenced commercial operations during FY2025-26 and forms part of the consolidated financial statements for FY2025-26. Share capital was subscribed on 24 April 2026. Shareholding is disclosed inconsistently: the AOC-1 table and the Board's report state 75%, while the AOC-1 preamble and the secretarial audit report describe it as a wholly owned subsidiary.
- Parul Dipak Patel — related party: Wife of the Managing Director Mr. Dipak Narendraprasad Patel and mother of the Executive Director Mr. Nirmit Dipak Patel. Re-appointment to an office or place of profit (employment) for a further five years with effect from 01-07-2026 was approved by the Board on 29 May 2026 on the Audit Committee's recommendation, and is put to members as a Section 188 special resolution (Item No. 6).
- Tansi Nirmit Patel — related party: Wife of the Executive Director Mr. Nirmit Dipak Patel and daughter-in-law of the Managing Director. Appointment to an office or place of profit (employment) for five years with effect from 01 April 2026 was approved by the Board on 29 May 2026 on the Audit Committee's recommendation, and is put to members as a Section 188 resolution (Item No. 7).

products.body: - **Specialty lipids:** Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil, High-purity specialty MCT grades (stated as under development), Customised and premium-grade MCT products (stated as proposed)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management states the outlook for the MCT Oil industry remains positive, with growing awareness of preventive healthcare, clinical nutrition and sports nutrition expected to drive sustained demand.
- Expansion in pharmaceutical manufacturing, increasing adoption of ketogenic diets and rising demand for functional ingredients are described as likely to provide significant growth opportunities.
- Growing demand from pharmaceutical and medical nutrition applications, coupled with increasing acceptance of clean-label ingredients, is expected to support long-term industry growth.
- India is described as emerging as an important manufacturing hub because of its expanding healthcare and food processing industries, with the Indian market presenting significant opportunity from pharmaceutical, nutraceutical and food processing growth plus increasing export potential.
- Increasing exports to North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific are listed as an opportunity, alongside expansion of the personal care and cosmetic industries and government initiatives promoting value-added specialty chemicals and food processing.
- Increasing consumer preference for healthier edible oils and specialty ingredients is cited as a demand driver.
- Management remains confident that upon successful commissioning the subsidiary will contribute meaningfully to long-term revenue growth and profitability - the entire growth narrative is contingent on a plant that has not yet been commissioned.
- Margin/cost narrative for the existing business: cost optimisation initiatives, efficient procurement practices and enhanced production planning are said to have contributed towards improved operating performance, and management states it remains committed to maintaining healthy profitability while pursuing sustainable growth.
- Named demand headwinds: volatility in coconut oil and palm kernel oil prices, supply chain disruptions and freight cost fluctuations, stringent international food safety and pharmaceutical quality standards, exchange rate fluctuations affecting export competitiveness, and increasing competition from global manufacturers.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Diversify out of the existing business into specialty chemicals and nutraceutical ingredients, executed through the newly incorporated subsidiary Oleo Biosciences Private Limited, Bengaluru, which is set up specifically to manufacture Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil.
- Complete the MCT Oil manufacturing project on schedule - procurement, purchase and installation of plant and machinery, utilities and other equipment - and commission it so commercial production starts in Q4 FY2026-27.
- Address both domestic and international markets on commissioning, with emphasis on the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, food and personal care industries.
- Expand manufacturing capacity.
- Develop high-purity specialty MCT grades and customised / premium-grade MCT products.
- Increase exports, with regulated international markets named as the export opportunity.
- Invest in research and development.
- Strengthen quality systems to comply with international standards such as GMP, HACCP, FSSC 22000 and ISO certifications - explicitly framed as a lever for the export ambition.
- Focus on value-added products and customer-specific formulations within the specialty lipid segment rather than commodity volume.
- Pursue potential strategic alliances with domestic and overseas customers.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The single expansion programme in this annual report is the Medium Chain Triglyceride (MCT) Oil manufacturing project. During FY2025-26 Crestchem incorporated Oleo Biosciences Private Limited, Bengaluru, on 31 March 2026 to implement it; the Board's report states an equity participation of 75%, while the secretarial audit report describes the same entity as a Wholly Owned Subsidiary. The subsidiary's registered office is at B-61/A, 2nd Cross, 3rd Stage, Peenya Small Industries, Bangalore North, Karnataka - 560058. The procurement, purchase and installation of plant and machinery, utilities and other manufacturing equipment is presently underway; management states the project is progressing in accordance with the implementation schedule. Subject to timely completion of installation, successful commissioning, statutory approvals and trial production, commercial production is expected to commence during the fourth quarter of FY2026-27. On commissioning the subsidiary proposes to serve both domestic and international markets, with emphasis on pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, food and personal care industries, and the Board expects the project to diversify the business portfolio and strengthen long-term growth prospects. Beyond this project the Company states a general intent to expand manufacturing capacity, develop high-purity specialty MCT grades and invest in research and development. No plant capacity, no project cost, no rupee capex quantum and no funding plan is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, and the Directors' report separately states there were no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position of the Company during the year.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Debt-free at the parent level: the secretarial auditor records that no secured loan has been obtained from any bank or financial institution and none of the Company's property has been mortgaged or hypothecated, confirmed through the MCA portal
- Entry into a high-value specialty lipid market with a stated positioning on value-added products and customer-specific formulations
- Promoter-led executive management with long tenure (Managing Director appointed 01/02/2008)
